title: Lane A P1 — Governed Checkpoint Authorization and Crash-Recovery Authority Closure
summary: Adds durable pre-commit authorization persistence and idempotent crash recovery to the standalone Checkpoint tool. Authorization receipts are now persisted to a JSONL ledger before any Git commit. Recovery reloads from the ledger and handles committed/unterminated states without duplicate authorization or duplicate commits. All seven gates proven with real Git repos.

The standalone Checkpoint tool validated authorization receipts in-memory but never persisted them to a durable ledger before executing the Git commit. If the process crashed between receipt validation and commit, the receipt was lost and recovery was impossible. The campaign checkpoint path (_campaign_checkpoint.py, _campaign_mutation.py) already had durable persistence and recovery, but the standalone tool lacked both. No parallel authority was needed — the existing auth_receipts.py infrastructure and JSONL ledger pattern could be reused.

Path: .build/rig-relay/governance/checkpoint_authorization_receipts.v1.jsonl. Append-only JSONL. Each record: receipt_digest, receipt_json, outcome, commit_sha, created_at. Persisted BEFORE the Git commit by _persist_authorization_receipt(). Loaded by _load_latest_authorization_receipt() for recovery.

Path: .build/rig-relay/governance/checkpoint_receipts.v1.jsonl. Append-only JSONL. Each record: receipt_digest, commit_sha, outcome, created_at. Distinct from the authorization ledger. Persisted after commit by _persist_terminal_checkpoint_receipt(). Checked by _has_terminal_receipt() for re-entry idempotency.

The Git commit carries the Rig-Authorization-Receipt-SHA256 trailer in its message body. The digest value is the receipt_sha256 from the authorization receipt JSON. Recovery uses _check_commit_for_receipt_trailer() which searches the last 10 commits for the matching trailer using git log --grep.

State 1: No auth receipt in ledger, no commit with matching trailer → Fresh authorization, persist, commit, terminal receipt
State 2: Auth receipt in ledger, no commit with matching trailer → Reuse existing authorization (A2), proceed to commit
State 3: Auth receipt in ledger, commit with matching trailer exists, no terminal receipt → Recovery: append terminal receipt (outcome: recovered), no new commit (A4)
State 4: Auth receipt in ledger, commit with matching trailer exists, terminal receipt exists → Re-entry: return existing outcome, no duplicate (A6)
State 5: Commit without matching authorization → Refused at _validate_preconditions (A3)
State A5: Mismatched authorization (wrong action, expired, invalid JSON) → Refused before any ledger persistence
All 84 existing checkpoint/governance/campaign/recovery tests pass alongside the 10 new tests. Zero regressions.

Durable pre-commit authorization persistence: authorization receipts are written to checkpoint_authorization_receipts.v1.jsonl before any Git commit
Distinct authorization/terminal ledgers: checkpoint_authorization_receipts.v1.jsonl (pre-commit) vs checkpoint_receipts.v1.jsonl (post-commit/recovery)
Commit-to-authorization binding: Rig-Authorization-Receipt-SHA256 trailer carries the receipt digest in commit messages
Idempotent recovery: reloads from ledger, handles all four states (fresh auth, reuse, commit-without-terminal, already-terminated)
Typed refusals: missing_receipt, invalid receipt JSON, expired receipt, action mismatch
Pre-extraction of receipt digest: recovery checks run before _validate_preconditions so committed states are detected before staging/guard failures
10 real-Git-repo tests covering all seven acceptance gates
Receipt digest consistency: tool now uses receipt_sha256 from receipt JSON rather than re-computing canonical digest, matching the auth_receipts generator
